Design work included maintaining parity with the ongoing visual refresh of [PlanetScale's web application](https://app.planetscale.com). Development work included migration from Gatsby to Next.js alongside Stitches.js as the styling framework.

In a 3-column layout, clicking on an image zooms it to take up space equal to last 2 columns. The image will overlay the in-page navigation but zooms out on scrolling out of view.

import Recipe from "../../components/recipe.astro";

<Recipe recipe="
>> servings: 1
>> time: 15 minutes

Roast 4 stalks of @asparagus{4%stalks} in a pan till suitably charred on all sides.
Finish off by splashing some water, and covering the pan on a low flame to steam the stalks.
Mix 1/2 cup of @cottage cheese{1/2%cup} with @salt{}, @pepper{}, and a squeeze of @lemon{}.
Cut a @baguette{} into the same length as the asparagus stalks. Slice in half and lightly toast.
Butter both slices, and spread the cottage cheese spread on one side.
Place the asparagus stalks on top of the spread and firmly close the sandwich with the other slice.
"/>

import Recipe from "../../components/recipe.astro";

<Recipe recipe="
>> servings: 1
>> time: 10 minutes

Grind the @green cardamom pods{2}, @black cardamom pod{1}, and @cloves{3}, coarsely preferably using a #mortar.
Add @ground black pepper{1/4 tsp}, and @nutmeg{1/4 tsp} to the spice mix.
Put @water{1%cup}, and @milk{1/3%cups} in a #saucepan and put it on a low flame.
Add @CTC tea{2%tsp}, @sugar{3%tsp}, @star anise{1}, @cinnamon stick{1/2}, and the spice mix into the saucepan.
Turn up heat, and wait til liquid boils up.
Reduce heat to make sure the liquid does not boil over.
Repeat previous 2 steps twice and then put it on simmer for a 5 minutes.
Use a strainer to filter out the tea."/>

import Recipe from "../../components/recipe.astro";

<Recipe recipe="
>> servings: 1
>> time: 2 minutes

Generously @butter{} 2 slices of @white bread{2%slices}.
On one of the now buttered slice, put a copious amount of @sea salted potato chips{}.
Use the other buttered slice to close the sandwich while crushing the chips such that the sandwich sits flat on both sides."/>

import Recipe from "../../components/recipe.astro";

<Recipe recipe="
>> servings: 1
>> time: 5 minutes

Peel a single @mango{1}, cut into chunks, and put into a blender.
Add 1 cup of @europan style yogurt{1%cup} to the blender.
Add a sprinkle of @cardamom powder{}, 1tsp of @vanilla{1%tsp}, and @honey{} to taste.
Blend until smooth.
"/>

import Recipe from "../../components/recipe.astro";

<Recipe recipe="
>> servings: 1
>> time: 5 minutes

Fry 2 @eggs{2} sunny side up.
As the eggs are cooking, scoop out 1 @avocado{1} into a bowl.
Add 4 tablespoons of @greek yogurt{4%tbsp} and mash together.
Season with @salt{to taste}, @pepper{to taste}, and a teaspoon of @turmeric{1%tsp}.
Optionally, add 2 tablespoons of @kimchi{2%tbsp}.
Once the eggs are done, place them on top of the avocado mix.
Top up with a handful of @potato chips{1%handful}.
"/>

<Recipe recipe="
>> servings: 1
>> time: 15 minutes

Toast 2 slices of @bread{2%slices}.
Take one slice and spread butter, and layer 6 thin slices of @soppressata sausage{6%slices}.
Top with a thin layer of @feta cheese{}.

Firmly close the sandwich.

One of the interesting situations to come out of being aware, and categorizing / naming fear as an underlying motivational factor while making decisions is this: What happens when two opposing decisions in a situation are both fear driven? It's either an incorrect categorization which is possible since the skill of naming fear is releatively new, or it's the classic between a rock and a hard place situation. And so, either the skill needs to be further practised and subsequently honed or the only way out is something akin to BATNA.
